# Authentication and Authorization Design
# Generated by @Architect for T004 task
# Date: 2026-04-15
# Based on contract.yaml security section

## 1. Overview

This document outlines the authentication and authorization design for the Booking System. The system uses JWT-based authentication with Passport.js strategies and implements Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) with fine-grained permissions.

## 2. Authentication Architecture

### 2.1 JWT Token Strategy

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Authentication Flow                       │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ 1. User submits credentials (email/password)                 │
│ 2. Server validates credentials against database             │
│ 3. Server generates:                                         │
│    - Access Token (JWT, 15 min expiry)                      │
│    - Refresh Token (JWT, 7 day expiry, stored in HttpOnly)  │
│ 4. Tokens returned to client                                 │
│ 5. Client includes Access Token in Authorization header      │
│ 6. Server validates token on each request                    │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### 2.2 Token Specifications

#### Access Token
```typescript
interface AccessTokenPayload {
  sub: string;      // User ID
  email: string;    // User email
  role: string;     // User role (USER, ADMIN)
  iat: number;      // Issued at
  exp: number;      // Expiration time (15 minutes)
  type: 'access';   // Token type
}
```

#### Refresh Token
```typescript
interface RefreshTokenPayload {
  sub: string;      // User ID
  tokenId: string;  // Unique token identifier
  iat: number;      // Issued at
  exp: number;      // Expiration time (7 days)
  type: 'refresh';  // Token type
}
```

### 2.3 Token Storage

- **Access Token**: Client-side memory (not localStorage/sessionStorage)
- **Refresh Token**: HttpOnly cookie with Secure and SameSite=Strict flags
- **Token Blacklist**: Redis for revoked tokens (logout, password change)

## 3. Passport Strategies

### 3.1 JWT Strategy

```typescript
// src/modules/auth/strategies/jwt.strategy.ts
@Injectable()
export class JwtStrategy extends PassportStrategy(Strategy) {
  constructor(configService: ConfigService) {
    super({
      jwtFromRequest: ExtractJwt.fromAuthHeaderAsBearerToken(),
      ignoreExpiration: false,
      secretOrKey: configService.get('JWT_SECRET'),
    });
  }

  async validate(payload: any) {
    // Validate user exists and is active
    const user = await this.usersService.findById(payload.sub);
    if (!user || !user.active) {
      throw new UnauthorizedException('User not found or inactive');
    }
    
    return {
      id: user.id,
      email: user.email,
      role: user.role,
    };
  }
}
```

### 3.2 Local Strategy (Email/Password)

```typescript
// src/modules/auth/strategies/local.strategy.ts
@Injectable()
export class LocalStrategy extends PassportStrategy(Strategy) {
  constructor(private authService: AuthService) {
    super({
      usernameField: 'email',
      passwordField: 'password',
    });
  }

  async validate(email: string, password: string) {
    const user = await this.authService.validateUser(email, password);
    if (!user) {
      throw new UnauthorizedException('Invalid credentials');
    }
    return user;
  }
}
```

## 4. Authorization - RBAC Design

### 4.1 Role Definitions

| Role | Description | System Permissions |
|------|-------------|-------------------|
| **USER** | Regular customer | Create/view own bookings, View services, Update profile |
| **ADMIN** | System administrator | All USER permissions + User management, Service management, System configuration |

### 4.2 Permission Matrix

#### User Permissions
| Permission | USER | ADMIN | Description |
|------------|------|-------|-------------|
| `user:read:own` | ✅ | ✅ | Read own user profile |
| `user:update:own` | ✅ | ✅ | Update own user profile |
| `user:read:any` | ❌ | ✅ | Read any user profile |
| `user:update:any` | ❌ | ✅ | Update any user profile |
| `user:delete:any` | ❌ | ✅ | Delete any user |
| `user:role:update` | ❌ | ✅ | Update user role |

#### Service Permissions
| Permission | USER | ADMIN | Description |
|------------|------|-------|-------------|
| `service:read` | ✅ | ✅ | View available services |
| `service:create` | ❌ | ✅ | Create new service |
| `service:update` | ❌ | ✅ | Update existing service |
| `service:delete` | ❌ | ✅ | Delete service |
| `service:toggle` | ❌ | ✅ | Activate/deactivate service |

#### Booking Permissions
| Permission | USER | ADMIN | Description |
|------------|------|-------|-------------|
| `booking:create` | ✅ | ✅ | Create new booking |
| `booking:read:own` | ✅ | ✅ | View own bookings |
| `booking:read:any` | ❌ | ✅ | View any booking |
| `booking:update:own` | ✅ | ✅ | Update own booking |
| `booking:update:any` | ❌ | ✅ | Update any booking |
| `booking:cancel:own` | ✅ | ✅ | Cancel own booking |
| `booking:cancel:any` | ❌ | ✅ | Cancel any booking |

#### Time Slot Permissions
| Permission | USER | ADMIN | Description |
|------------|------|-------|-------------|
| `timeslot:read` | ✅ | ✅ | View available time slots |
| `timeslot:create` | ❌ | ✅ | Create new time slots |
| `timeslot:update` | ❌ | ✅ | Update time slots |
| `timeslot:delete` | ❌ | ✅ | Delete time slots |

### 4.3 Permission Checking Implementation

```typescript
// src/common/decorators/permissions.decorator.ts
export const Permissions = (...permissions: string[]) => 
  SetMetadata('permissions', permissions);

// src/common/guards/permissions.guard.ts
@Injectable()
export class PermissionsGuard implements CanActivate {
  constructor(private reflector: Reflector) {}

  canActivate(context: ExecutionContext): boolean {
    const requiredPermissions = this.reflector.get<string[]>(
      'permissions',
      context.getHandler(),
    );

    if (!requiredPermissions) {
      return true;
    }

    const { user } = context.switchToHttp().getRequest();
    const userPermissions = this.getUserPermissions(user.role);
    
    return requiredPermissions.every(permission => 
      userPermissions.includes(permission)
    );
  }

  private getUserPermissions(role: string): string[] {
    const rolePermissions = {
      USER: [
        'user:read:own',
        'user:update:own',
        'service:read',
        'booking:create',
        'booking:read:own',
        'booking:update:own',
        'booking:cancel:own',
        'timeslot:read',
      ],
      ADMIN: [
        // All USER permissions
        'user:read:own',
        'user:update:own',
        'service:read',
        'booking:create',
        'booking:read:own',
        'booking:update:own',
        'booking:cancel:own',
        'timeslot:read',
        // Admin-only permissions
        'user:read:any',
        'user:update:any',
        'user:delete:any',
        'user:role:update',
        'service:create',
        'service:update',
        'service:delete',
        'service:toggle',
        'booking:read:any',
        'booking:update:any',
        'booking:cancel:any',
        'timeslot:create',
        'timeslot:update',
        'timeslot:delete',
      ],
    };

    return rolePermissions[role] || [];
  }
}
```

## 5. Security Guards Implementation

### 5.1 JWT Auth Guard (Global)

```typescript
// src/common/guards/jwt-auth.guard.ts
@Injectable()
export class JwtAuthGuard extends AuthGuard('jwt') {
  canActivate(context: ExecutionContext) {
    return super.canActivate(context);
  }

  handleRequest(err, user, info) {
    if (err || !user) {
      throw err || new UnauthorizedException('Invalid or expired token');
    }
    return user;
  }
}
```

### 5.2 Roles Guard

```typescript
// src/common/guards/roles.guard.ts
@Injectable()
export class RolesGuard implements CanActivate {
  constructor(private reflector: Reflector) {}

  canActivate(context: ExecutionContext): boolean {
    const requiredRoles = this.reflector.get<string[]>(
      'roles',
      context.getHandler(),
    );

    if (!requiredRoles) {
      return true;
    }

    const { user } = context.switchToHttp().getRequest();
    return requiredRoles.includes(user.role);
  }
}
```

### 5.3 Combined Guard Usage

```typescript
// Example controller usage
@Controller('bookings')
@UseGuards(JwtAuthGuard)
export class BookingsController {
  
  @Get()
  @UseGuards(RolesGuard)
  @Roles('USER', 'ADMIN')
  findAll(@Req() req) {
    // Both authenticated and has USER or ADMIN role
  }

  @Post()
  @UseGuards(PermissionsGuard)
  @Permissions('booking:create')
  create(@Body() createBookingDto: CreateBookingDto) {
    // Authenticated and has booking:create permission
  }

  @Get(':id')
  @UseGuards(PermissionsGuard)
  @Permissions('booking:read:own', 'booking:read:any')
  findOne(@Param('id') id: string, @Req() req) {
    // Additional logic to check if user owns the booking
    // unless they have booking:read:any permission
  }
}
```

## 6. Security Middleware

### 6.1 Helmet Configuration

```typescript
// src/main.ts
import helmet from 'helmet';

async function bootstrap() {
  const app = await NestFactory.create(AppModule);
  
  // Security headers
  app.use(helmet({
    contentSecurityPolicy: {
      directives: {
        defaultSrc: ["'self'"],
        styleSrc: ["'self'", "'unsafe-inline'"],
        scriptSrc: ["'self'"],
        imgSrc: ["'self'", "data:", "https:"],
        connectSrc: ["'self'"],
        fontSrc: ["'self'"],
        objectSrc: ["'none'"],
        mediaSrc: ["'self'"],
        frameSrc: ["'none'"],
      },
    },
    hsts: {
      maxAge: 31536000,
      includeSubDomains: true,
      preload: true,
    },
    xFrameOptions: { action: 'deny' },
    xContentTypeOptions: true,
    xXssProtection: true,
  }));
  
  await app.listen(3001);
}
```

### 6.2 CORS Configuration

```typescript
// src/main.ts
app.enableCors({
  origin: process.env.CORS_ORIGIN?.split(',') || ['http://localhost:4200'],
  credentials: true,
  methods: ['GET', 'POST', 'PUT', 'DELETE', 'PATCH', 'OPTIONS'],
  allowedHeaders: ['Content-Type', 'Authorization', 'X-Requested-With'],
  exposedHeaders: ['Authorization'],
});
```

### 6.3 Rate Limiting

```typescript
// src/app.module.ts
import { ThrottlerModule } from '@nestjs/throttler';

@Module({
  imports: [
    ThrottlerModule.forRoot([{
      ttl: 60000, // 1 minute
      limit: 100, // 100 requests per minute
    }]),
  ],
})
export class AppModule {}
```

## 7. Password Security

### 7.1 Password Hashing

```typescript
// src/common/utils/password.util.ts
import * as bcrypt from 'bcrypt';

export class PasswordUtil {
  static async hash(password: string): Promise<string> {
    const saltRounds = 12;
    return bcrypt.hash(password, saltRounds);
  }

  static async compare(
    password: string,
    hashedPassword: string,
  ): Promise<boolean> {
    return bcrypt.compare(password, hashedPassword);
  }
}
```

### 7.2 Password Policy

- Minimum length: 8 characters
- Must contain at least one uppercase letter
- Must contain at least one lowercase letter  
- Must contain at least one number
- Must contain at least one special character
- No common passwords (check against common password list)
- No sequential characters (e.g., "12345", "abcde")
- No repeated characters (e.g., "aaaaaa")

## 8. Session Management

### 8.1 Token Refresh Flow

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Token Refresh Flow                       │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ 1. Access token expires (15 min)                            │
│ 2. Client sends refresh token (HttpOnly cookie)             │
│ 3. Server validates refresh token:                          │
│    - Checks signature                                       │
│    - Checks expiry                                          │
│    - Checks blacklist                                       │
│ 4. If valid, generates new access token                     │
│ 5. Optionally rotates refresh token                         │
│ 6. Returns new access token                                 │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### 8.2 Token Revocation (Logout)

```typescript
// src/modules/auth/auth.service.ts
@Injectable()
export class AuthService {
  constructor(private redisService: RedisService) {}

  async logout(userId: string, refreshTokenId: string) {
    // Add refresh token to blacklist (24 hour TTL)
    await this.redisService.set(
      `blacklist:refresh:${refreshTokenId}`,
      userId,
      'EX',
      24 * 60 * 60, // 24 hours
    );
    
    // Optionally blacklist current access token
    // (requires storing token IDs in access tokens)
  }
}
```

## 9. Audit Logging

### 9.1 Authentication Events

| Event | Log Level | Data Captured |
|-------|-----------|---------------|
| Login Success | INFO | User ID, IP, User Agent, Timestamp |
| Login Failure | WARN | IP, User Agent, Attempted Email, Reason |
| Logout | INFO | User ID, IP, Timestamp |
| Token Refresh | INFO | User ID, Old Token ID, New Token ID |
| Password Change | INFO | User ID, IP, Timestamp |
| Role Change | INFO | User ID, Old Role, New Role, Changed By |

### 9.2 Authorization Events

| Event | Log Level | Data Captured |
|-------|-----------|---------------|
| Permission Denied | WARN | User ID, Required Permission, Resource, IP |
| Admin Action | INFO | Admin User ID, Action, Resource, Changes |

## 10. Security Testing

### 10.1 Authentication Tests

- **Unit Tests**: Password hashing, token generation/validation
- **Integration Tests**: Login flow, token refresh, logout
- **Security Tests**: Brute force protection, token tampering, CSRF protection

### 10.2 Authorization Tests

- **Unit Tests**: Permission checking logic
- **Integration Tests**: Role-based access, permission-based access
- **Penetration Tests**: Privilege escalation attempts

## 11. Compliance Requirements

### 11.1 GDPR Compliance
- User consent for data processing
- Right to access, rectify, erase data
- Data portability
- Privacy by design

### 11.2 OWASP Top 10
- A01:2021 - Broken Access Control
- A02:2021 - Cryptographic Failures  
- A07:2021 - Identification and Authentication Failures

### 11.3 PCI DSS (if handling payments)
- Secure transmission of card data
- Tokenization of sensitive data
- Regular security testing
